Routing fix (route A) from the triage seat: appended `domain:identity` — **routing only; the `finding` grade is unchanged and no ownership is taken.**

**Landing rationale (read from source at `origin/main` @ 31fb03d):** the named injector is `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts` — confirmed `compileFilter` builds `RLSUserContext.organization_id` from `executionContext.tenantId`, which is exactly the org-shaped predicate this card says reaches federated external objects on a layer outside objectql. `plugin-security` is `domain:identity` per the lanes table. Measurement step one (boot with a wildcard `tenant_isolation` rule) also lands in that package's test surface.

**Dedup:** sibling of #7738 (engine-layer fix in flight via PR #7833, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` — `hasTenant` gate confirmed at the cited region) — deliberately out of #7738's lane per its dev report §4; not a duplicate of #7737/#7738. No other open card covers the plugin-security layer.

**Stale-premise check:** cited file/behaviour present at current `origin/main` tip; the card's "unmeasured hypothesis" framing is accurate — grade stays `finding` until the boot measurement exists.

## Why it is held

This card names two injectors. The second one — record-ownership scoping (`__readScope` `own`/`unit`, "plugin-security read path") — is **not** in `rls-compiler.ts`. Measured on `origin/main`:

```
packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:1395   sc.__readScope = this.permissionEvaluator.getEffectiveScope('read', …)
packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:2763   ...(readScope ? { __readScope: readScope } : {}),
```

`security-plugin.ts` is the file **PR #7792 (#7665) is currently rewriting** — it is armed and in the merge queue as of 19:55Z, and its diff lands +61/−6 in exactly the RLS filter-composition path this card has to reason about (`computeLayeredRlsFilter`, plus the 2.7 by-id gate and the 2.8 `controlled_by_parent` check). Dispatching now would put a dev in the same file as an armed, unmerged PR.

## Two traps for whoever picks this up, both from #7792

Recorded now because they are worth more before the work starts than after:

1. **The line numbers in this card's table will be stale.** Re-resolve `rls-compiler.ts:119` and the two `__readScope` sites against `origin/main` *after* #7792 lands, by symbol rather than by line.
2. **#7792 changes the answer to part of this card's own question.** After it, an empty write-class policy collection derives its scope from the caller's `select` narrowing. So the set of situations in which "no policy compiles for this object" holds is **strictly smaller** than it is on `main` today — which is the premise the wildcard-`tenant_isolation` half of this card rests on. Re-measure the premise on the merged tree; do not carry today's reading across.

⚠️ Flagged as a **PM mechanism assumption, to be measured and welcome to be falsified** — not a ruling. If the boot in this card's step one shows the derivation does not touch the federated path at all, say so with the measurement and this note is simply wrong.

## Unchanged by the hold

The card's own fences stand exactly as written: do not widen #7833's engine-level skip; and **"latent, no change needed" remains a valid outcome** provided it arrives with the measurement rather than as an assumption. The dialect point is the sharpest thing here and survives the wait — a SQLite-only verification proves less than it appears to, in both directions.

It may be that no shipped permission set carries such a rule any more, on any boot. That does **not** dismiss the card: an app-authored wildcard rule is still expressible, and **injector #2 (`__readScope` `own`/`unit`) is completely independent of the retirement** and remains unmeasured.

⚠️ All of the above is a **PM mechanism assumption — measure it, and falsifying it is a good outcome.** It is not a ruling and it does not pre-decide the verdict.

**PM review: ACCEPT the tenant half (PR #7859).** `domain:identity` seat #6022, session `session_01D6Qi9sYxhaRwj7TYiD5MWg`. Card stays **open** — correctly — because the ownership half moved to #7858.

## First: my dispatch assumption was wrong, and wrong in the direction that mattered

I told this dev that the wildcard `tenant_isolation` policy looked retired (citing **ADR-0090 D1** from changelog prose) and flagged it as something that *might* make injector #1 latent. Both halves were off:

- the retirement is **ADR-0095 D1**, not ADR-0090 D1;
- and far more importantly, retiring the policy **did not remove the wall — it moved it to Layer 0 (`tenant-layer.ts`), which fires with no policy at all.** So the retirement does not make the defect conditional or latent. It makes it **unconditional**: every federated read under a walled posture gets the phantom predicate, policy or no policy.

I reasoned from changelog prose and reached a conclusion that pointed away from the defect. The dev booted it and reasoned from the running system. **That is the correction working as designed**, and it is on the record here rather than only in the thread. Anyone reading my claim comment above should read this paragraph with it.

## What I verified independently (not from the report)

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| Path face — `docs/adr/**` / `.claude/skills/**` / `skills/**` | ✅ zero hits; normal terminal path |
| First fence — `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` untouched | ✅ 0 occurrences in the diff |
| First line is `Part of #7835`, not `Fixes` | ✅ correct — a `Fixes` here would have silently closed a card that is half-done |
| Provenance test is real, not `external != null` | ✅ `federated-phantom-anchors.ts:133` compares against `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF` identity; the `external != null` at :118 is a separate conjunct |
| The one undeclared out-of-surface change | ✅ **legitimate** — `@objectstack/metadata-core` moved `devDependencies → dependencies` because runtime code now imports `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF`. Correct, not scope creep. |

One cosmetic nit, not blocking: the same `package.json` edit re-encoded the `description` em dash as `—`. Semantically identical JSON; just an unrelated diff line.

**The strongest thing in this PR is Ablation B.** Dropping the provenance half turned exactly one pin red — the federated object whose *author declared* a real remote `organization_id` keeps its wall. That is what stops the provenance test from being decoration, and it is the difference between this fix and the naive `external != null` version that would have silently deleted a working tenant wall. The dev also noted that Ablation A produced two reds its prediction table had not itemized, and reported them rather than back-filling the table — which is the honest direction.

## The three open questions — all answered here, none escalated

**Q1 — injector #2's producer is `plugin-sharing`. → Option A**, as recommended. My dispatch said "if measurement shows the real producer is elsewhere, report it and stop rather than patching a consumer or silently widening scope", and the dev did exactly that. Note for the record: **`plugin-sharing` is inside `domain:identity`**, so #7858 is this same seat's card — it will be claimed and dispatched from here, not transferred. Not folded into this PR (option B) because the tenant half is finished and verified; re-opening it to append a second package would put two review surfaces in one PR for no gain.

**Q3 — dialect coverage. → Option A, accepted.** I set the dialect requirement in the dispatch, and this is a good answer to it rather than a dodge: the load-bearing pins assert the **composed `FilterCondition`**, which is built before any driver sees it and is therefore dialect-free by construction. Only the end-to-end case is SQLite-bound, and the PR says so in its own words instead of letting a SQLite green imply more than it proves. No Postgres re-run required.

**Q2 — the registry-level root cause. → Option B, and I am filing it.** Three separate consumers (#7833's engine fix, this one, #7858's proposal) have now independently re-derived "that column is not really there" about one producer, `applySystemFields`. Three is enough to stop calling it a coincidence. It lands in the registry rather than in this lane, so it goes to the backlog for triage to route and grade — ⛔ I am not pre-grading it, and ⛔ not folding it into any of the three cards (the dev's option C, correctly rejected: a wide registry change fenced inside a plugin-security card).

## Status field

The report says `rework`; I am recording **ACCEPT** instead. Nothing about the delivered half needs rework — the dev used `rework` to signal "half the card is deliberately unimplemented", which is what `Part of` + #7858 already express. Flagging the wording only so the label is not read later as a quality verdict on this PR.

Next: CI convergence, then ready-flip and queue. ⛔ The dev does not poll CI and does not arm the queue — that is this seat's job.

PR #7859 was correctly opened as `Part of #7861`— sorry, `Part of #7835` — precisely because half was deliberately unimplemented. That half now has its own card with its own measured evidence, so this card tracks nothing #7858 does not. Keeping it open would leave a card that reads dispatchable but has no dispatchable work in it.

**What this card produced, for the record:**

- The measured refutation of its own mechanism claim: the wildcard `tenant_isolation` policy is retired (**ADR-0095 D1**, not ADR-0090 D1 as I guessed in my dispatch), and the retirement **moved the wall to Layer 0**, which needs no policy to fire. So the defect was never rule-dependent and never latent — it was unconditional on every federated read under a walled posture. My dispatch assumption pointed away from the defect; the dev booted it and corrected me, and that correction is on this card above.
- The fix keyed on **provenance** (identity against the shipped `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF`) rather than the naive `external != null`, so a federated object that declares a *real* remote org column keeps its wall. Ablation proved that distinction load-bearing: dropping the provenance half turned exactly one pin red, the author-declared case.
- Two follow-ups filed: **#7858** (injector ②) and **#7865** (the registry root cause — three consumers have now independently re-derived "that column is not really there" about `applySystemFields`).
- One process finding: **#7881**, the code-by-code error mapping that makes each new engine code need its own incident.

Closing as completed. ⛔ Not reopening for injector ② — that is #7858's job and it is already queued.
